name: Western Australia Construction & Quoting
description: Domain context for residential and rural construction quoting in the Perth Hills and Keysbrook corridor. Informs cost language, supplier context, permit awareness, and quote structure for Nexus analysis prompts.
voice: Grounded, practical, straight-talking. WA trade pricing, local supplier relationships, and rural site conditions shape every number. No city-centre markup assumptions.

quoting.payment_preference: PayID (instant bank transfer), then BSB/account, then card as fallback
quoting.deposit_structure: 10% on quote acceptance (fully refundable before materials ordered), 40% on materials delivery, 40% on practical completion, 10% retention released 30 days post-handover

labour_rates.note: Indicative rates for the Perth Hills / Keysbrook corridor. Confirm per engagement.

common_line_items: Site preparation and access (rural sites typically +15–25% on metro rates)
Footings and slab (Class M/H reactive clay soils common in hills corridor)
Roof cladding (Colorbond preferred — heat tolerance, fire zone compliance)
Wall cladding (fibre cement or brick veneer; BAL rating may apply)
Electrical rough-in and fit-off (Western Power connection or off-grid)
Plumbing rough-in and fit-off (scheme water or rainwater/bore supply)
Insulation (bulk + reflective, NCC Section J compliance)
Septic or ATU system (common in Keysbrook — no reticulated sewer)
Driveway and hardstand (gravel common; bitumen if council required)
Landscaping and revegetation (black cockatoo habitat consideration where applicable)
exclusions_standard: Council and building permit fees (quoted separately at cost)
WAPC or bushfire attack level (BAL) assessment fees
Contaminated soil removal (advise if history of fuel/chemical storage)
Utility connection fees (Western Power, Water Corporation)
Engineering certificates beyond standard residential scope

regulatory.bushfire_note: BAL assessment required for most rural lots. BAL-12.5 to BAL-40 typical in hills corridor. BAL-FZ possible in dense jarrah.
regulatory.heritage_note: Nil for standard rural residential — flag if near registered Aboriginal heritage sites.
regulatory.environmental_note: Vegetation clearing permit may be required (DBCA). Avoid disturbance to identified black cockatoo nesting/foraging habitat where practicable.

suppliers.note: Preferred local supply chain for cost accuracy and lead time reliability.
suppliers.timber_frame: Wesbeam (Jandakot), BGC Timber, or Carter Holt Harvey via local merchants
suppliers.roofing: Lysaght Colorbond (BlueScope) — stocked at Bowens or Midland Brick
suppliers.concrete: Boral or Hanson — batching plants at Mundijong / Byford corridor
suppliers.plumbing_electrical: Reece Plumbing (Armadale), Rexel or Middy's Electrical (Armadale / Rockingham)

analysis_hints: When reviewing construction quotes or cost breakdowns, flag any line item missing GST disclosure.
Rural site preparation costs are frequently under-estimated — challenge any slab quote that doesn't itemise soil classification.
Prefer payment schedules tied to physical milestones over calendar dates.
Bushfire attack level (BAL) compliance is non-negotiable and can add 5–20% to external cladding and glazing costs.
Septic/ATU systems in Keysbrook typically cost AUD 12,000–22,000 installed; flag if absent from rural build quotes.
Black cockatoo foraging trees (marri, wandoo, banksia) should be preserved where site layout allows — aligns with sanctuary vision.
sanctuary_link: This domain pack directly informs physical infrastructure on the Keysbrook sanctuary land. Quoting accuracy here funds and shapes the habitat restoration mission.
